items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: And the show was owned by Arnold Rothstein, he was the great gambler, you know. ... He was a gangster, you know, Arnold Rothstein.

ctx.x: No, they they were the stars of the show because I had -- I did a stint with them when they had Shuffle Along in New York -- that was in 1920. Incidentally, we went

over that, we passed by that. But I played part -- I played a few weeks in that show, but I didn't want to be tied down to a show because I couldn't have no fun sitting in a pit. If I could be on stage I could have a ball on stage. And this Keep Shuffling -- I joined them and went on the road with that show. We did 17, 18 weeks in New York, then we went on the road with it. And the show was owned by Arnold Rothstein, he was the great gambler, you know. So, while we were in Chicago he was murdered at Park Central…
In those days, it's like during the period you were in Chicago, Chicago was fairly active, though.
